programming_tips.description: The INTEGREX i-200 supports both MAZATROL conversational programming and EIA/ISO G-code. MAZATROL mode uses process-based programming (UNIT/SEQUENCE) where you define operations (face, OD rough, bore, mill) and the control generates toolpaths. EIA mode uses standard G-code. Programs can mix modes — call an EIA subprogram from MAZATROL or vice versa. Use MAZATROL for standard turning/milling operations and EIA for complex multi-axis or custom macro work.
gotchas: MAZATROL and EIA programs have different file extensions — do not rename
Tool offset numbering differs between modes
G96/G97 behavior in EIA requires explicit G50 clamp that MAZATROL handles automatically

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.code_example:
G05 P10000 (SMOOTH Mode 1: high-quality surface finish)
G01 X_ Y_ Z_ F2000
...
G05 P0 (cancel SMOOTH mode)
programming_tips.description: SmoothX SMOOTH Machining activates AI-based path planning. Mode 1 (P10000): prioritizes surface quality with intelligent jerk control — use for finish milling and contouring. Mode 2 (P20000): balanced — good for semi-finish. Mode 3 (P30000): prioritizes speed — use for roughing. SMOOTH modes pre-analyze the entire program and optimize acceleration profiles block-by-block.
gotchas: SMOOTH modes require sufficient look-ahead buffer — avoid very short blocks (<0.01mm)
Cancel SMOOTH mode (G05 P0) before turning operations
SMOOTH Mode 1 may reduce feed rate by 10-20% on tight radii — account in cycle time estimates

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.code_example:
G05.1 Q1 (activate VAC)
G01 X_ Z_ F_ (turning or milling moves)
G05.1 Q0 (deactivate VAC)
programming_tips.description: VAC uses AI to optimize axis acceleration and jerk in real-time based on commanded path geometry and machine dynamics. It smooths axis transitions, reduces vibration, and improves surface finish without sacrificing cycle time. Especially effective on B-axis interpolation moves and complex 5-axis toolpaths.
gotchas: VAC adds slight processing overhead — minimal impact on cycle time
VAC must be activated per program, not persistent across programs
Best results when combined with SMOOTH Mode 1 for 5-axis work

programming_tips.topic: B-Axis Interpolation Milling on Turned Surfaces
programming_tips.code_example:
G43.4 H01 (TCPC on)
G68.2 X0 Y0 Z0 I0 J90.0 K0 (tilt plane 90deg for OD milling)
G01 X_ Y_ Z_ B_ C_ F_ (simultaneous 5-axis)
G69 (cancel tilted plane)
G49 (cancel TCPC)
programming_tips.description: The INTEGREX B-axis enables milling at any angle from -120 to +120 degrees. For 3+2 positioning: use G68.2 to establish a tilted work plane, then mill normally. For simultaneous 5-axis: use G43.4 (TCPC) so the control maintains tool tip position as B and C axes move. This enables features like helical grooves on turned diameters, angled holes, and complex sculptured surfaces on shaft parts.
gotchas: Always verify B-axis angle limits — collision with chuck at extreme angles
TCPC (G43.4) requires accurate tool length and tool center point data in offset table
B-axis resolution is 0.0001 deg but practical accuracy depends on clamping force — unclamp (M13) for interpolation, clamp (M12) for positioning

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.topic: G12.1 Polar Coordinate Interpolation for Face Milling
programming_tips.code_example:
G97 S1500 M03 (fixed RPM for milling)
M19 (orient spindle for C-axis)
G12.1 (polar interpolation ON)
G42 D01 (cutter comp right)
G01 X50.0 C0 F200
X30.0 C90.0
...
G40 (cancel cutter comp)
G13.1 (polar interpolation OFF)
programming_tips.description: G12.1 converts C-axis rotation and X-axis linear moves into polar interpolation on the face of a turned part. This enables milling flat features (pockets, slots, text) on the face of a part held in the chuck without needing the Y-axis. The X-axis becomes the radial direction and C-axis becomes the angular direction. Essential for face features that exceed Y-axis travel (230mm).
gotchas: Must use G97 (constant RPM), NOT G96 (CSS) — spindle is in C-axis positioning mode
X=0 creates a singularity — avoid programming through the spindle center
Feed rate in G12.1 is at the tool tip, not at the programmed radius — actual surface speed varies

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.topic: G107 Cylindrical Interpolation for OD Features
programming_tips.code_example:
G97 S800 M03
M19
G107 C50.0 (cylindrical mapping on 50mm radius)
G01 Z_ C_ F_ (mill along cylinder surface)
G107 C0 (cancel cylindrical interpolation)
programming_tips.description: G107 maps a flat (ZC) plane onto a cylindrical surface of the specified radius. This enables milling flat-bottom slots, engraving text, or cutting spline features on the OD of a turned part. The Z-axis provides axial motion while C-axis wraps around the cylinder. The C value in G107 specifies the mapping radius.
gotchas: Mapping radius MUST match actual part radius — mismatch causes depth errors
Tool diameter must be small enough for the curvature — large endmills cut deeper at edges on small diameters
Feed rate is tangential at the specified radius — actual chip load varies with tool position

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.code_example:
M200 (open main chuck)
(Sub-spindle advances, grips part)
M211 (close sub-chuck)
(Main chuck releases)
M201 (close main chuck on empty)
G14 (program relative to sub-spindle)
(Machine second-op features)
G15 (return to main spindle)
programming_tips.description: On INTEGREX i-200S and i-200ST models, the sub-spindle enables complete done-in-one machining. After first-op turning/milling on the main spindle, the sub-spindle advances, grips the part, the main chuck opens, and the sub-spindle retracts to machine the second operation. G14/G15 switch programming reference between spindles. MAZATROL conversational mode handles handoff automatically in a SUB-SPINDLE UNIT.
gotchas: Match chuck pressures — excessive sub-spindle pressure deforms thin-wall parts
Verify concentricity after handoff — measure runout on sub-spindle before cutting
Program a facing cut on sub-spindle to clean up the bar cutoff witness mark
G14 reverses Z-axis direction — +Z moves away from sub-spindle chuck face

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.code_example:
(After turning:)
G97 S0 M05 (stop main spindle)
M19 (orient for C-axis mode)
(Now safe to command C-axis or milling)
T0800 M06 (load milling tool)
G97 S3000 M203 (start milling spindle CW - B-axis head)
G43.4 H08 (TCPC on)
programming_tips.description: Switching between turning and milling modes requires careful sequencing. Before milling: cancel G96 (CSS), stop main spindle, orient with M19 to engage C-axis mode, then start milling spindle. Before turning: stop milling spindle, retract B-axis to safe angle (B0), unload milling tool, load turning tool on turret, cancel G43.4 TCPC, then engage G96.
gotchas: NEVER start milling spindle while main spindle is in G96 CSS mode — creates collision risk
Cancel G43.4 (TCPC) before returning to turning — TCPC modifies axis positions
Retract B-axis to B0 before turret index — turret collision zone
Always verify which spindle is active before commanding S and M03/M04

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.topic: SMOOTH AI Machining — Intelligent Pocket Strategy
programming_tips.description: SmoothX includes AI-assisted pocket milling that automatically optimizes toolpath engagement angle and feed rate within MAZATROL conversational programs. When defining a POCKET UNIT in MAZATROL, the control generates trochoidal-style paths in corners and maintains constant chip load. This reduces cycle time by 15-30% compared to conventional zig-zag pocket milling and dramatically improves tool life.
gotchas: AI pocket strategy only available in MAZATROL conversational mode, not in EIA G-code
Requires SMOOTH Machining license option
Best results with solid carbide endmills — does not optimize for indexable insert tools

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.code_example:
G54.4 P1 (activate setup error comp set 1)
G01 X_ Z_ F_ (cutting moves — WCS corrected for tilt/shift)
G54.4 P0 (deactivate setup error comp)
programming_tips.description: G54.4 corrects for workpiece misalignment by applying measured position and angle offsets. After probing the part on the main or sub-spindle, the control calculates XYZ shift and angular tilt, storing these in a compensation set. This allows machining accurately without re-fixturing. Especially useful for second-op work on the sub-spindle where concentricity may be imperfect.
gotchas: Requires probing system to populate compensation values
Only corrects linear shifts and rotations — not for warped or bent parts
Large angular corrections (>2 deg) may exceed axis travel on Y-axis

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.description: The INTEGREX i-200 lower turret has 12 VDI stations. Standard turning tools use VDI 40 holders (OD, boring, grooving, threading). Live tooling stations accept driven tool holders for cross-drilling, milling, and tapping from the turret (independent of the upper milling spindle). Tool data must include holder type, projection, and whether it is a driven or static tool.
gotchas: Driven tools on the turret have lower RPM and power than the milling spindle — use milling spindle for demanding operations
Turret collision check does not account for non-standard holder projections — verify manually
Live tool stations require coolant through the turret — verify connections

source.handbook_title: Mazak INTEGREX i-200 Operation Manual H740-SA-0010E Rev C

programming_tips.topic: Safe EIA Program Start Block for INTEGREX
programming_tips.code_example:
O0001 (PROGRAM NAME - INTEGREX i-200)
G15 (main spindle selected)
G40 G49 G80 G54 G90 G97 S0
(G15=main spindle, G40=cancel comp, G49=cancel TCPC,
 G80=cancel cycles, G54=WCS1, G90=absolute, G97=RPM mode)
programming_tips.description: Every EIA program on the INTEGREX should start with a safety block that cancels modal states. Include G15 to ensure main spindle is selected, G49 to cancel any TCPC, G80 to cancel canned cycles, G40 to cancel cutter comp, G97 to disable CSS. This prevents carryover from a previous MAZATROL or EIA program.
